# SK1070 — Deconstruct the tuple instead of reading it element by element

<!-- Generated from Rules/Rikarin.Skala.Rules.Metadata/rules.json. Do not edit. -->

Consecutive `var` declarations read every element of one tuple in order, which is a deconstruction written out longhand.

| | |
|---|---|
| Category | Modernization |
| Default severity | suggestion |
| Scope | Semantic |
| Needs a compilation | yes |
| Fix | yes, safe |
| Language version floor | 7.0 |
| Since | 1.3 |

## Why

Deconstruction arrived with tuples in C# 7 and is the form the language was given the tuple for; a model writes the `Item1`/`Item2` reads because most of its training data is older than both. The longhand form also loses the one thing the tuple was carrying — that the pieces belong together — and `var a = t.Item1;` names the variable twice while naming what it holds not at all.

## Example

Instead of:

```csharp
var pair = Split(text);
var key = pair.Item1;
var value = pair.Item2;
```

Write:

```csharp
var pair = Split(text);
var (key, value) = pair;
```

## When it does not fire

⚠ **Deconstruction evaluates the receiver once and the longhand form evaluates it once per element, so the receiver has to be something re-reading cannot observe.** The rule requires it to be a single identifier naming a *local or a parameter*: reading one N times and reading it once are then the same program by construction, which is a stronger claim than the usual "no invocation in the path" and is the reason no property or field receiver is matched. ⚠ **A partial deconstruction is not this rule.** Every element of the tuple must be read, exactly once, in positional order, by consecutive single-declarator statements — `var a = t.Item1;` on its own is one variable with a name, not a deconstruction missing three quarters of itself. ⚠ **Every declaration must be `var`.** `var (a, b) = t;` gives each variable the element's type; a written type on one of the longhand declarations means the author asked for a different type, and reproducing that needs the typed deconstruction form the fix does not emit. ⚠ Only real tuple types — `System.ValueTuple` and its language syntax — are matched. `System.Tuple<T1, T2>` deconstructs only through the `System.TupleExtensions` extension methods, so the rewrite would depend on a `using` the file may not have. ⚠ Declarations carrying modifiers, attributes, `const`, `using`, `await` or `ref` are excluded, as is any run whose span holds a comment or a preprocessor directive, because the fix deletes those lines.
